title: Dhuska with Chana Dal
steps: Soak rice and chana dal, grind into a slightly coarse batter with green chilli, ginger and salt. Ferment briefly if desired.
Heat oil and deep-fry spoonfuls of batter into thick, golden, crispy discs.
Serve hot with ghugni, potato curry or chutney.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Iconic Jharkhand breakfast and street snack – crisp outside, soft inside.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Best eaten fresh from the oil.

title: Dhuska with Urad Dal
steps: Soak rice and urad dal, grind into a slightly coarse batter with green chilli, ginger and salt. Ferment briefly if desired.
Heat oil and deep-fry spoonfuls of batter into thick, golden, crispy discs.
Serve hot with ghugni, potato curry or chutney.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Iconic Jharkhand breakfast and street snack made with urad dal.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Crisp outside, soft inside.

title: Chilka Roti with Chana Dal
steps: Soak rice and chana dal overnight. Grind into a smooth batter and add salt.
Heat a tawa, grease lightly, pour and spread the batter into a thin pancake. Cook both sides till golden.
Serve with chutney, vegetable curry or meat curry.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Traditional rice-and-chana dal pancake of the Chotanagpur region.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Light yet filling.

title: Chilka Roti with Urad Dal
steps: Soak rice and urad dal overnight. Grind into a smooth batter and add salt.
Heat a tawa, grease lightly, pour and spread the batter into a thin pancake. Cook both sides till golden.
Serve with chutney, vegetable curry or meat curry.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Traditional rice-and-urad dal pancake of the Chotanagpur region.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Light yet filling.

title: Litti Chokha
steps: Prepare spiced sattu stuffing with mustard oil and aromatics. Stuff into wheat dough balls and seal.
Roast over charcoal or bake till the crust is crisp and slightly charred.
Make chokha by roasting and mashing brinjal, tomato and potato with onion, green chilli and mustard oil.
Dip hot littis in ghee and serve with chokha.

fullIngredients.name: Sattu, mustard oil, garlic, ginger, green chilli, ajwain, lemon, salt
Onion, green chilli, mustard oil for chokha

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Shared with Bihar but equally iconic in Jharkhand – rustic, smoky and satisfying.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Traditional open-fire roasting is ideal.

title: Rugda (Rugra) Curry
steps: Clean the rugda thoroughly. Heat mustard oil, sauté onion, garlic and chilli.
Add the mushrooms, turmeric and salt. Cook till tender and well-flavoured.
Serve with rice – a seasonal forest delicacy.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, garlic, green chilli, turmeric, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Wild mushroom prized in Jharkhand tribal cuisine – available mainly in the monsoon/early winter.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Simple preparation highlights the natural flavour.

title: Ghugni with Black Chickpeas
steps: Pressure-cook the soaked black chickpeas. Prepare a spicy onion-tomato gravy with mustard oil.
Add the chickpeas and simmer. Garnish with onion, green chilli, coriander and lemon.
Serve hot, often with muri (puffed rice) or as a side.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, tomato, ginger, green chilli, spices
Mustard oil, lemon, coriander for garnish

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Everyday protein-rich curry made with black chickpeas.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Often eaten with puffed rice as muri-ghugni.

title: Ghugni with White Peas

Add the peas and simmer. Garnish with onion, green chilli, coriander and lemon.
Serve hot, often with muri (puffed rice) or as a side.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, tomato, ginger, green chilli, spices
Mustard oil, lemon, coriander for garnish

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Everyday protein-rich curry made with white peas.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Often eaten with puffed rice as muri-ghugni.

title: Dal Pitha
steps: Cook and grind spiced chana dal into a filling. Make a soft rice-flour dough.
Stuff, shape into parcels and steam (often in leaves) till cooked.
Serve with green chutney or mustard dip.

fullIngredients.name: Ginger, garlic, green chilli, cumin, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Steamed rice-flour dumplings with spiced dal – light and traditional winter dish.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Similar to Bihari versions but firmly part of Jharkhand home cooking.

title: Jharkhandi Mutton Curry
steps: Marinate mutton with yogurt and spices. Sauté onion and ginger-garlic in mustard oil.
Add the mutton and cook till tender in a rich, spiced gravy.
Serve with rice or roti – common at celebrations and in non-tribal as well as tribal homes.

fullIngredients.name: Garam masala, red chilli, turmeric, mustard oil

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Hearty meat curry – mustard oil gives the characteristic aroma.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Slow cooking is preferred.

title: Koinar Saag
steps: Wash and chop the koinar leaves. Heat mustard oil, add crushed garlic and chilli.
Add the greens and salt. Stir-fry till just wilted and flavourful.
Serve as a simple side with rice.

fullIngredients.name: Garlic, green chilli, mustard oil, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Popular local leafy green of Jharkhand – nutritious and everyday.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Minimal cooking preserves nutrients and colour.

title: Thekua
steps: Melt jaggery with a little water. Mix into wheat flour with ghee and cardamom to form a stiff dough.
Shape into discs (use traditional moulds if available) and deep-fry on medium heat till golden and crisp.
Cool and store. Especially made for Chhath Puja.

fullIngredients.name: Oil or ghee for deep frying

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Iconic Chhath festival sweet shared with Bihar – crisp, mildly sweet and long-lasting.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Ghee in the dough improves flavour.

title: Arsa Roti
steps: Soak rice, grind into a paste. Cook jaggery into a thick syrup and mix with the rice paste.
Shape into small discs and deep-fry till golden and crisp.
Cool and store. A festive sweet.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Traditional rice-jaggery sweet of the region – made during festivals.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Crisp exterior with sweet interior.

title: Bhaat Dal with Toor Dal & Saag
steps: Cook rice and a simple tempered toor dal.
Prepare a side of seasonal saag stir-fried with garlic and green chilli in mustard oil.
Serve the everyday Jharkhandi plate of rice, dal and greens with pickle.

fullIngredients.name: Seasonal saag (greens) with garlic, green chilli, mustard oil

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The daily meal of most households – simple, balanced and rice-centric.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Mustard oil is the preferred cooking medium.

title: Tribal-style Pork Curry
steps: Cut pork into pieces. Sauté onion, garlic, ginger and chilli in mustard oil.
Add the pork and cook slowly till tender, using minimal water so the meat cooks in its own fat and juices.
Season simply. Serve with rice – common in many tribal communities.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Pork is widely eaten in tribal Jharkhand – preparations are often simple and robust.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Slow cooking on low heat yields the best texture.
